string-array.name: help_rpm
string-array.item: Crankshaft speed. The ECU calculates it from the crankshaft position sensor.
On this car, 615 rpm was seen at warm idle in P. After a cold start RPM is higher and comes down as the engine warms up.
Noticeably \"hunting\" at warm idle — check per-cylinder misfires on the \"Fuel\" tab and the fuel trims. We don\'t know the exact allowed fluctuation for this engine.

string-array.name: help_speed
string-array.item: Vehicle speed as the engine ECU sees it.
The speedometer usually reads slightly above actual speed. The best check is to compare with GPS speed at a steady pace.
Consistently differs from GPS — non-standard tire size: then mileage and L/100km are off too.

string-array.name: help_coolant
string-array.item: Coolant temperature from the engine sensor.
We don\'t know the exact thermostat opening and fan-on temperatures for this engine. Note where the gauge needle sits on a warm car and compare against that.
Takes long to warm up — possibly a thermostat stuck open (the ECU then usually sets P0128). Keeps rising without stopping — a cooling problem: coolant level, fans, water pump.

string-array.name: help_load
string-array.item: Calculated load (per the OBD standard): what share of the maximum possible air the engine is drawing in right now.
Low at idle, close to 100% at full throttle. At altitude it\'s lower at full throttle: the air is thinner. We have no exact figures for this car.
This one is mostly for comparing across sessions: if at full throttle and the same RPM it\'s lower than before, the engine is short of air (air filter, MAF, throttle).

string-array.name: help_throttle
string-array.item: Throttle position (absolute). The ECU controls the throttle from the pedal signal — electronic throttle.
With this PID a closed throttle usually doesn\'t read 0%, and wide open may not read 100% — that\'s how it\'s measured. We don\'t know this car\'s values yet: check min/max after a drive.
Jumps while the pedal is still, or the ECU goes into limp mode — the throttle body or its sensors (codes P2135, P2101).

string-array.name: help_pedal
string-array.item: Accelerator pedal position, sensor D. The pedal has two independent sensors (D and E), and the ECU constantly cross-checks them.
As with the throttle, a released pedal doesn\'t read 0%, and floored doesn\'t read 100%. For this car\'s actual values, check min/max after a drive.
Jumps while your foot is still — the pedal assembly or its connector (D/E sensor correlation code — P2138). Sensor E is on the \"All data\" tab; it should move in step with D.

string-array.name: help_timing
string-array.item: Ignition timing advance in degrees before top dead center. The ECU reduces it when it detects knock.
Depends on RPM and load. We don\'t have this engine\'s ignition maps, so there\'s no numeric norm.
Look at it together with knock retard on the \"Fuel\" tab: if there is often retard, the ECU is fighting knock (fuel, overheating). The retard formulas are unverified.

string-array.name: help_maf
string-array.item: Mass air flow from the MAF sensor, in grams per second. The ECU bases its fuel calculation on it.
We have no reference values for this engine. Most useful is to note your own value at warm idle and compare with it in later sessions.
Lower than usual at idle, with fuel trims on both banks gone positive — the classic picture of a dirty MAF or an air leak after it.

string-array.name: help_map
string-array.item: Intake manifold absolute pressure. Shows the vacuum the engine creates.

With the engine off and ignition on, it equals atmospheric pressure (compare with \"Baro pressure\"). At idle it\'s far below atmospheric, at full throttle almost equal to it. We don\'t know the exact idle figure for this car — note your own.
Noticeably higher than usual at warm idle — weaker vacuum: air leak, valve timing, compression.

string-array.name: help_iat
string-array.item: Intake air temperature.
Slightly above outside temperature while driving. In traffic and after parking with a hot engine it\'s noticeably higher, and drops quickly once moving.
Shows −40 °C — usually an open sensor circuit: that\'s the bottom of the scale.

string-array.name: help_runtime
string-array.item: Time since engine start, in seconds. Resets on every start.
Just a counter. Useful when reviewing a session: the first minutes are warm-up, when mixture and RPM behave differently.
Reset to zero while driving — the engine stalled or the ECU rebooted.
